cards.subject: Gordok Commons
lines: The ogres named this wing. The elves did not.
The Gordunni squat in ruined Highborne halls and hold court in them — the throne, the prisoner, the drinks vendor and the tribute chest all sit in somebody else's architecture.

cards.subject: Two ways to stand here
cards.tag: The honest run and the quiet one
lines: Kill everything and take normal boss loot. Or hug the walls, thread the patrols, freeze one guard and talk another into walking off.
Same instance, two completely different games.
It is decided in the first corridor.

cards.subject: The loot counts what you did not kill
lines: Killing the king spawns a chest, and every named ogre still breathing when he falls adds a guaranteed item to it.
Clear the wing properly and it holds potions and food. Leave them all alive and it holds gear.
It is the one vanilla dungeon where restraint is the loot table.

cards.subject: Freeing the goblin locks you out of the suit
lines: He is chained in the Halls of Destruction. A shackle key off the ogres frees him and he leaves a cache of three-hundred-skill leatherworking and tailoring patterns behind.
But once he is gone he is gone.
He is also the only one who will trade you the ogre suit. Do the suit first.

cards.subject: The suit is a playable race that never happened
lines: It reuses ogre animations built while Blizzard was still considering ogres for the Horde. The idea was dropped.
What survived is a ten-minute costume with joke flavour text: "It lifts AND supports!"
Try /dance in it.

cards.subject: The basket is a trap
lines: The suit needs tannin, and it is in a basket at the back of the first balcony, up the ramp.
Taking it spawns a Gordok Bushwacker on top of you.
On a tribute run, one careless pull here is the whole run.

cards.subject: You do not fight him. You gossip.
lines: Wearing the suit, you can walk up to him and mention that Guard Fengus has been talking.
"Hey, who Fengus callin' a gnoll lover?! Take da prisoners to da king..."
He stomps off to settle it — leaving his post, and leaving himself alive for the tribute.

cards.subject: He buffs you from inside the ice
lines: He tinkers with broken traps. Repair the frost trap on his patrol and it takes him, and he stays frozen for the rest of the run.
Once you are king he will happily talk to you and hand out Slip'kik's Savvy.
Still inside the block of ice.

cards.subject: A boss who is a bar
lines: He blinds you with Booze Spit until you are king. After that he is a vendor with a menu — Gordok Green Grog, Kreeg's Stout Beatdown, Volatile Rum.
The only boss in the place whose defeat condition is arguably buying a drink off him instead.

cards.subject: Two heads, hired for it
lines: The king's advisor is a two-headed ogre mage, on the theory that two heads would be twice as resourceful. He heals the king through the fight.
Spare him and he flips instantly.
"Uh... I sorry I attack you boss. You no kill me, please OK?!"

cards.subject: Whoever kills the king becomes the king
cards.tag: It is a mechanic, not a metaphor
lines: Cho'Rush shouts "The king is dead - OH NOES! Summon Mizzle da Crafty!"
Mizzle has waited in the throne room through the whole fight. He inspects the body — "Yar, he's dead all right" — and hands you the crown.
The survivors go friendly and start selling you things.

cards.subject: Raiders came for three ogres they refused to kill
lines: Once you are king the three surviving guards buff you — attack power, stamina, spell crit, two hours each.
Molten Core and Blackwing Lair rosters ran tribute the way they ran flasks.
This dungeon's real endgame value was three ogres left standing.

cards.subject: The crown does not travel
lines: The title belongs to whoever holds the room. Walk out of Dire Maul and the ogres pick somebody else.
Every run, the crown changes hands and changes back inside the hour.
